title: The Door serves read and position inside its scope, as MACHINE_PROTOCOL version 2
summary: @inventarch/runtime: the Door accepts two new operations, read and position. read takes params {within?, locator, includeRuntime?} and answers {ok: true, result} with the ReadBody readBody returns ({locator, identity, kind, path?, digest, body, certified: false}) or that function's read refusal. It always reads through a scope token, the initial boundary when within is omitted. Through a token narrower than the whole workspace, one bound to a root below the workspace root, a phase or identities, or issued under such a token (the scope operation issues one when it is given any of them, and a door opened with a boundary that sets one starts with one), a locator that no admitted record in the scope answers, whether its record is outside the scope, refused by admission or absent, is one plain IA-RUNTIME-READ-UNADMITTED, 'The locator is not in this scope', which names no path, line, identity or refused record. Through a whole-workspace token, one that @inventarch/db isCompleteScope proves complete (the initial token of a door opened without a boundary, as the MCP door's is, or with one that sets none of them, and a token the scope operation issues from such a token without setting any), a miss is refused as readBody refuses it without a token: a record admission refused is named with its path, line and reason, an identity no source holds is not in this workspace's sources, and a line says what the workspace's sources hold in its file. The door reads documents through the new DoorOptions.read, by default @inventarch/db readWorkspaceBytes over its root bounded at 4 MiB, and names a document it cannot read by its workspace-relative path, never by the server's root: a root that can no longer be opened, as when the workspace moves while the door serves, is refused IA-RUNTIME-READ-UNREACHABLE, as every failure of the reader is, its message carrying the default reader's IA-DB-ROOT-INVALID, 'The workspace can no longer be opened to read <path>', which names the document alone. It binds adopted mounts once, when it opens, from .ia/workspace.json, unless it was opened with explicit adopted captures, which name no directory. ReadBodyOptions gains an optional within: given a scope token, readBody reads get and records in that scope and refuses every miss in a narrower scope with that plain refusal, and every miss in a whole-workspace one as it refuses it without a token. ReadRefusal gains an optional reason, admission's reason, on the refusal of an identity whose record admission refused, read without within or through a whole-workspace token; without within readBody is otherwise unchanged. position takes params {within?, seat?, shape?, phase?, depth?, budget?, word?} and answers {ok: true, result} with the {body, digest, hostNote} that position returns for that partial key through the door's scope token, byte for byte: no params is K0, and the other parts take normalizeScopeKey's defaults. Request text, a token or any other parameter is refused as an unknown parameter, so nothing text-driven runs. A refusal of the key is {ok: false, code: IA-RUNTIME-REQUEST-INVALID, message, next}, next naming one command: ia position --shape <context|governance|execution|sequence|learning> or ia position --phase <orient|plan|act|learn> for a part outside its closed set, ia position --depth 2 or ia position --budget 64 for a part outside its cap, ia vocabulary for a word that is no string or that the closure does not register, ia position for a seat of another form, a seat the scope does not admit or a path outside the workspace, and for a seat at runtime placement ia position, or ia inspect when that seat is the one K0 takes, the repository's own `@workspace`, whether the key names it or not. RuntimeError gains an optional next, which normalizeScopeKey and resolveScopeKey now set on each key refusal they throw, so position throws it too; the code and message of every refusal are unchanged. The new DoorOptions.protocol is the MACHINE_PROTOCOL version a door serves, by default the current one: a door at version 1 refuses read and position as the unknown operation 1.1.0 refused, byte for byte, and a value that is not an integer from 1 to the current version is a TypeError. A version 1 operation's refusal, and every refusal the Door raises itself, keep 1.1.0's {ok, code, message}. MACHINE_PROTOCOL is version 2: ProtocolOperation gains an optional since, absent on the nine version 1 rows, whose JSON is byte-identical to 1.1.0's; the read row is appended with since: 2 and mcp: ia_read, and the position row, after next, with since: 2 and mcp: ia_position, each with one flow line. Code that expects MACHINE_PROTOCOL.version to be 1, reads every row as a CLI machine route, or pins the version 2 rows or their parameters should filter the rows by since or take the new rows. A version 2 door's unknown-operation refusal lists read, next and position, in that order, after the version 1 operations it admits. @inventarch/db exports readWorkspaceBytes(root, path, limit), which returns one workspace file's exact bytes and refuses a path that escapes the workspace, is not portable by the rule the distribution workspace file reader applies (NFC, at most 1024 code units, no backslash, control character or any of <>:"|?*, no segment that ends in a dot or a space or names a reserved device) or passes a link or junction, and a hard-linked or nonregular file (IA-DB-PATH-UNSAFE), a missing or unreadable file or one of more than limit bytes (IA-DB-SOURCE-UNAVAILABLE), and a file replaced or resized during the read (IA-DB-SOURCE-CHANGED); each refusal names the file by its canonical path alone. @inventarch/mcp-door serves ia_read and ia_position, whose inputSchemas are the read and position rows' params, so with ia_next it serves twelve tools. @inventarch/cli: runCli, the machine route that @inventarch/cli/internal/main exports and the host launcher's door mode calls, opens its door at protocol version 1, so read and position there are refused with exactly 1.1.0's bytes; in @inventarch/cli/internal/operation-help, describeOperation describes only the version 1 rows, and renderOperationSchema and renderOperationHelp label a version 1 row's description version 1, as 1.1.0 did, whatever the table's version, and a later row, should a caller hand them one, the version its since names. Limits: the CLI's machine routes stay the nine version 1 operations, so ia scope in every form, the other routes, their help and their --schema output are unchanged, and ia read stays the consumer verb, which returns the Door's body and digest and refuses a document the Door refuses with the same code, though its own reader names a link by its absolute local path; ia position, the consumer verb of the same output, runs the ia position commands its refusals name.
